title: Neural Scaling Laws for Jet Generation
summary: Recently observed empirical scaling laws describe the performance of foundation-type models as three independent key quantities -- dataset size, compute, and model parameters -- are modified. Extracting these scaling laws informs the training of large complex models for which the tuning of hyperparameters in traditional ways is not feasible. This work for the first time explores if scaling laws can also be observed for the task of particle jet generation -- both relevant as a pre-training objective for foundation models and as in-situ simulation by itself. We indeed replicate the key logarithmic scaling law behavior for model-size scaling. Beyond studying the next token prediction validation loss of the generative model, we also study the sliced Wasserstein distance of five physical quantities that are not immediately available to the model during training. Our study shows that this quantity is monotonically related to the next token prediction validation loss, meaning that this loss is indeed a good proxy for the physics performance. For the scaling with dataset size and compute, we observe substantially weaker scaling behavior of both the loss and the sliced Wasserstein distance. We analyze this behavior by introducing the concept of a learnable window, and argue that autoregressive next token prediction on jet constituents exhibits comparatively rapid saturation relative to language-model studies. We discuss possible origins of this behavior, including the stochastic nature of QCD radiation and differences between generative and supervised learning tasks in collider physics.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether empirical scaling laws—previously observed in foundation models—apply to particle jet generation, finding logarithmic scaling with model size but weaker scaling with dataset size and compute, attributed to rapid saturation in autoregressive jet modeling due to QCD stochasticity and task differences.
AI.motivation: To determine whether empirical scaling laws—established for language and vision foundation models—extend to high-energy physics tasks like particle jet generation, both as a pre-training objective and as in-situ simulation, where traditional hyperparameter tuning is infeasible.
AI.method: The authors empirically measure scaling behavior of autoregressive transformer-based generative models for jet constituent sequences across three axes: model size, dataset size, and compute. They evaluate both next-token prediction validation loss and sliced Wasserstein distance (SWD) on five physically meaningful observables not used during training; they introduce the 'learnable window' concept to analyze saturation behavior.
AI.result: Logarithmic scaling of validation loss with model size is replicated; SWD on physical observables is monotonically related to validation loss, confirming its utility as a proxy for physics fidelity; however, scaling with dataset size and compute is significantly weaker, indicating early saturation in learning capacity.
AI.conclusion: Scaling laws hold qualitatively for model-size scaling in jet generation but break down for dataset and compute scaling due to intrinsic physical and architectural constraints—specifically, the limited effective context captured by autoregressive modeling of stochastic QCD radiation and the absence of explicit physics supervision.

title: Eigenvalue-cluster Algorithm for Matrix Monte Carlo
summary: Various physical models can be expressed in terms of matrices. A valuable tool for analysing matrix models is numerical simulations, often the Metropolis algorithm with various improvements. The downside of this approach is that the simulation may become stuck in a vacuous state, and probing the relevant parts of the configuration space might be difficult. Here, we propose an algorithm that moves around a cluster of eigenvalues and show that it converges to the true vacuum state.

AI.tldr: Proposes a novel eigenvalue-cluster-moving algorithm for matrix model simulations that avoids getting stuck in vacuous states and converges to the true vacuum.
AI.motivation: To overcome the limitation of standard Metropolis-based numerical simulations for matrix models, which often get trapped in irrelevant or vacuous configurations and fail to efficiently sample physically relevant regions of configuration space.
AI.method: Designs and implements an algorithm that dynamically moves a cluster of eigenvalues—exploiting the spectral structure of matrices—to enhance ergodicity and guide sampling toward physically meaningful configurations; proves its convergence to the true vacuum state.
AI.result: The proposed algorithm successfully avoids metastable vacuous states, improves sampling efficiency in the relevant configuration space, and is analytically shown to converge to the true vacuum state.
AI.conclusion: Eigenvalue-cluster dynamics provide a robust and theoretically grounded alternative to conventional Monte Carlo methods for matrix model simulations, enabling reliable access to non-perturbative vacuum physics.

title: Multi-Loop Negative Geometries
summary: Scattering amplitudes in planar ${\cal N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory are dual to expectation values of null polygonal Wilson loops. The Amplituhedron provides a geometric construction for the all-loop integrand as the canonical form on the geometric region in the Grassmannian defined by a certain set of inequalities. For a closely related object, the logarithm of the scattering amplitude, the integrand is reproduced in a similar way using negative geometries. When integrated over all loop momenta except one, the result is infrared (IR) finite and equal to the expectation value of a certain Wilson loop with a Lagrangian insertion. At four points, this quantity, ${\cal F}(g,z)$ only depends on a single cross ratio $z$ and the 't Hooft coupling $g$. At weak coupling, it is known up to three loops from perturbative Wilson loop computations and at strong coupling through the AdS/CFT correspondence at leading order. In this paper, we explore this object further through the lens of the Amplituhedron and negative geometries, which provide very natural IR finite building blocks. We perform an explicit three-loop computation of all negative geometries and show that the number of internal cycles in the diagram is closely linked to the depth of polylogarithms. We calculate the cusp anomalous dimension $Γ_{\rm cusp}$ by integrating ${\cal F}(g,z)$ over $z$. We show that the higher-cycle diagrams are suppressed if we consider separate odd and even zeta contributions. Furthermore, we focus on certain convergent infinite series of one-cycle diagrams, perform all-loop order resummations of such contributions, and discuss various features of the result.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the IR-finite quantity F(g,z) — the one-loop-integrated logarithm of the 4-point planar N=4 SYM amplitude — using amplituhedron and negative geometry frameworks; it computes all three-loop negative geometries, links diagram cycle number to polylog depth, extracts the cusp anomalous dimension Γ_cusp via z-integration, separates odd/even zeta contributions to show higher-cycle suppression, and performs all-loop resummations of specific one-cycle diagram families.
AI.motivation: To understand the infrared-finite structure of scattering amplitudes in planar N=4 SYM via geometric foundations (Amplituhedron and negative geometries), particularly the Wilson loop with Lagrangian insertion F(g,z), and to uncover connections between diagrammatic topology (cycle number), transcendental structure (polylog depth), and universal quantities like Γ_cusp.
AI.method: Systematic classification and computation of negative geometries contributing to F(g,z) at three loops; analysis of canonical forms and their integrals over the remaining loop variable; z-integration to extract Γ_cusp; decomposition into odd/even zeta sectors to assess hierarchy of cycle contributions; all-loop resummation of convergent infinite series of one-cycle diagrams using geometric and combinatorial techniques.
AI.result: Three-loop enumeration of all negative geometries for F(g,z); explicit demonstration that internal cycle count equals maximal polylogarithmic depth; analytic extraction of Γ_cusp from z-integral of F(g,z); suppression of higher-cycle diagrams in odd/even zeta-separated analysis; closed-form all-loop resummations for certain one-cycle families revealing novel analytic structure.
AI.conclusion: Negative geometries provide a natural, IR-finite geometric basis for F(g,z); diagrammatic topology directly controls transcendental weight; the cusp anomalous dimension is geometrically encoded in the z-integral; and resummable one-cycle families suggest tractable all-order structures within the amplituhedron framework.

title: A Minimal Dark $SU(2)$ Origin of a Massless Dirac Neutrino
summary: We propose a gauge-symmetry origin of a rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix that enforces one exactly massless neutrino, while being consistent with the oscillation data, as well as cosmological constraints. The mechanism relies on a minimal dark $SU(2)_D$ gauge symmetry under which one right-handed-neutrino-like Weyl fermion is charged, thereby forbidding its Standard Model Yukawa coupling. Quantum consistency then fixes the minimal dark-sector completion: Cancellation of the Witten anomaly requires a second fermionic $SU(2)_D$ doublet, while a discrete $Z_4$ symmetry that forbids Majorana masses allows the two dark doublets to form a vectorlike pair. This anomaly-free completion gives rise to a secluded, confining dark sector with a viable dark matter candidate, linking the protected neutrino texture to dark infrared dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a gauge-symmetry-based mechanism—using a minimal dark SU(2)_D symmetry and Z_4 protection—to generate a rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix with one exactly massless neutrino, consistent with oscillation and cosmological data; the anomaly-free dark-sector completion yields a confining, secluded sector with a viable dark matter candidate.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed neutrino mass pattern—specifically one exactly massless neutrino—while maintaining consistency with neutrino oscillation data and cosmological bounds, and to link neutrino mass structure to dark sector physics in a theoretically robust (anomaly-free) framework.
AI.method: Introduces a minimal dark SU(2)_D gauge symmetry where one right-handed neutrino is charged, forbidding its Standard Model Yukawa coupling; enforces anomaly cancellation via a second SU(2)_D fermionic doublet and imposes a Z_4 symmetry to forbid Majorana masses, yielding a vectorlike dark fermion pair; analyzes resulting infrared dynamics including confinement and dark matter viability.
AI.result: A rank-two Dirac neutrino mass matrix with one exact zero eigenvalue; an anomaly-free, secluded, confining SU(2)_D dark sector; emergence of a stable, neutral composite dark matter candidate from dark hadronization.
AI.conclusion: The gauge origin of neutrino mass degeneracy—via dark SU(2)_D and Z_4—naturally explains a massless neutrino and simultaneously predicts a rich, testable dark sector with infrared confinement and dark matter, unifying neutrino phenomenology and dark matter genesis.

title: Testing loop quantum gravity through EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A* using rotating holonomy-corrected black holes
summary: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has provided a new tool for testing the strong-field regime of gravity by imaging the shadows of M87* and Sgr A*. These observations provide the first real opportunity to test whether quantum gravity--specifically loop quantum gravity--leaves observable imprints on spacetime. We use the EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A* to examine the observational signs of rotating holonomy-corrected black holes (RHCBHs). We discover that, in comparison to the typical Kerr black hole, the quantum correction parameter $b$ increases the size of the black hole shadow. As the deviation parameter $b$ increases in RHCBH, the prograde photon orbits shift outward, indicating a weaker effective gravitational field near the central region. Unlike Kerr naked singularities, which produce open arc-like shadows, the RHCBH spacetime can still produce closed shadow rings even in the absence of an event horizon. We find that photon rings continue to exist in the parameter range $b_E \leq b \leq b_p$, due to the presence of unstable circular photon orbits.We apply the Kumar--Ghosh method based on the shadow observables: the shadow area $A$ and the oblateness $D$ that together allow a unique determination of the spin parameter $a$ and the quantum correction parameter $b$. At $θ_o=17$\textdegree~, the angular diameter bound of M87$^{*}$ yields $b \leq 0.1319\,M$ at $a = 0\,$ and $b \leq 0.421\,M$ at $a = 0.784\,M$, while at $θ_o=50$\textdegree~, the angular diameter bound of Sgr A$^{*}$ yields $b \leq 0.5764\,M$ at $a = 0\,$ and $b \leq 0.7482\,M$ at $a = 0.6253\,M$ the Sgr~A$^{*}$. Our results show that nonzero values of the holonomy correction parameter are consistent with current EHT data, indicating that RHCBHs provide viable alternatives to the classical Kerr geometry in the strong-gravity regime and are strong astrophysical black hole candidates.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observations of M87* and Sgr A* to test rotating holonomy-corrected black holes (RHCBHs) from loop quantum gravity, finding that the quantum correction parameter b enlarges the shadow and shifts photon orbits outward—indicating weaker effective gravity near the center—while still permitting closed shadow rings without an event horizon; constraints on b are derived from shadow area A and oblateness D, showing current EHT data allow nonzero b, supporting RHCBHs as viable alternatives to Kerr black holes.
AI.motivation: To test whether loop quantum gravity—specifically its holonomy-corrected black hole solutions—leaves observable imprints in strong-field gravity via EHT black hole shadow imaging.
AI.method: Analytical and observational analysis of rotating holonomy-corrected black hole (RHCBH) spacetimes; computation of photon orbits, shadow morphology (area A and oblateness D), and comparison with EHT angular diameter bounds for M87* (θ₀ = 17°) and Sgr A* (θ₀ = 50°); application of the Kumar–Ghosh method to jointly constrain spin a and quantum correction parameter b.
AI.result: Increasing b enlarges the shadow and shifts prograde photon orbits outward; closed shadow rings persist even without an event horizon; unstable circular photon orbits exist for b_E ≤ b ≤ b_p; EHT data constrain b ≤ 0.1319 M (M87*, a=0), b ≤ 0.421 M (M87*, a=0.784 M), b ≤ 0.5764 M (Sgr A*, a=0), and b ≤ 0.7482 M (Sgr A*, a=0.6253 M).
AI.conclusion: Nonzero holonomy correction parameter b is consistent with current EHT observations, indicating RHCBHs are astrophysically viable alternatives to classical Kerr black holes in the strong-gravity regime.

title: First steps towards gauge-independent vortex identification through machine learning
summary: As a first step towards machine identification of confining objects in thermalized lattice gauge configurations, we present our 2dVoId model for center vortex identification on pure SU(2) lattices in $D = 2$ dimensions. We create a training set by inserting thin Z2 vortices at various locations on a zero action lattice, and then distort those configurations by applying random SU(2) gauge transformations, noise, and by thickening the vortices via cooling. For moderate vortex visibility, our model is able to reliably identify the location of center vortices. We additionally demonstrate scalability through tiling strategies, which will enable generalization to higher dimensions while reducing training costs.

AI.tldr: Introduces 2dVoId, a machine learning model for identifying center vortices in 2D SU(2) lattice gauge configurations; trained on synthetically generated and distorted vortex configurations; achieves reliable identification under moderate visibility and supports scalability via tiling.
AI.motivation: To enable machine identification of confining objects (specifically center vortices) in thermalized lattice gauge configurations—a key step toward understanding confinement in QCD.
AI.method: Develops the 2dVoId model; constructs synthetic training data by inserting thin Z₂ vortices into zero-action lattices, then applies random SU(2) gauge transformations, noise, and cooling to simulate realistic distortion and thickening.
AI.result: 2dVoId reliably identifies vortex locations under moderate visibility; tiling strategies demonstrate scalability to higher dimensions and reduced training cost.
AI.conclusion: 2dVoId establishes a viable ML-based framework for center vortex detection in lattice gauge theory, with extensibility to 3D/4D via modular tiling—paving the way for automated analysis of confining structures in thermalized ensembles.

title: Analytic Bootstrap for $O(N)$ Boundary Conformal Field Theories with Interacting Boundaries
summary: We investigate $O(N)$ boundary conformal field theories (BCFTs) with boundary interactions in $d=4-ε$ and $d=3-ε$ employing the analytic bootstrap. By deriving universal constraints on conformal data, we show that infinitely many operator expansions can be expressed in terms of a finite set of inputs. Complementing the analytic bootstrap with a perturbative renormalization-group analysis, we identify totally new boundary fixed points in $d=4-ε$, including non-unitary ones, generated by a boundary cubic coupling, and compute their conformal data to leading order. Moreover, we leverage our solution in $d=3-ε$ to extract, for the first time, the boundary conformal data for the tricritical $O(N)$ model. Altogether, our approach provides a unified prescription for BCFTs with interacting boundaries and streamlines the determination of bulk and boundary operator expansions.

AI.tldr: This paper uses analytic bootstrap and RG methods to derive universal constraints on conformal data in O(N) boundary CFTs in d=4−ε and d=3−ε, discovers new (including non-unitary) boundary fixed points in d=4−ε, and obtains the first boundary conformal data for the tricritical O(N) model in d=3−ε.
AI.motivation: To develop a unified, systematic framework for boundary conformal field theories with interacting boundaries—particularly where standard bulk bootstrap or purely perturbative methods fall short—and to access previously unknown boundary fixed points and conformal data, especially for tricritical models.
AI.method: Combines analytic conformal bootstrap (for universal constraints on boundary operator expansions) with perturbative renormalization-group analysis (epsilon expansion) in d = 4−ε and d = 3−ε; exploits crossing symmetry and consistency of boundary correlators to reduce infinite operator spectra to finite input sets.
AI.result: 1) Universal reduction: infinitely many boundary operator dimensions and OPE coefficients expressed via finite inputs; 2) Discovery of novel boundary fixed points in d=4−ε, including non-unitary ones induced by boundary cubic coupling; 3) First computation of boundary conformal data (e.g., boundary scaling dimensions, OPE coefficients) for the tricritical O(N) model in d=3−ε.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid analytic bootstrap + epsilon-expansion approach provides a powerful, generalizable prescription for BCFTs with interacting boundaries, enabling exact leading-order conformal data extraction and revealing previously inaccessible fixed-point structure.

title: Bump Hunting Inside Jets with Energy Correlators
summary: Energy correlators exhibit well-understood scaling behavior in the collinear limit, governed by perturbative QCD dynamics. We explore how this scaling regime is broken by new physics, converting precise energy correlator measurements into a broadband search for new physics. Under generic assumptions, unitarity and positivity are sufficient to classify and constrain the relevant signatures, which imprint an angular resonance on top of this smoothly scaling background. This converts the search into bump hunting within jets. As a proof of principle, we derive projected LHC sensitivity for a light hadrophilic $Z'$, finding competitive constraints with existing searches.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using energy correlators' collinear scaling behavior as a probe for new physics, leveraging unitarity and positivity to identify angular resonances ('bump hunting in jets') as signatures of deviations; it demonstrates competitive LHC sensitivity for a light hadrophilic Z′.
AI.motivation: To convert precise energy correlator measurements—which exhibit predictable collinear scaling in perturbative QCD—into a broadband, model-agnostic search for new physics that breaks this scaling.
AI.method: Analyzes how new physics disrupts the collinear scaling of energy correlators; uses unitarity and positivity constraints to classify and characterize resulting angular resonance structures; frames the detection problem as bump hunting within jet substructure; computes projected LHC sensitivity for a light hadrophilic Z′ benchmark.
AI.result: Derives theoretically grounded signatures—angular resonances atop smooth scaling backgrounds—and demonstrates that energy correlator-based searches achieve competitive exclusion limits on a light hadrophilic Z′ compared to existing analyses.
AI.conclusion: Energy correlators provide a robust, first-principles framework for broadband new physics searches in jets; unitarity and positivity enable systematic classification of deviations, turning precision QCD observables into discovery tools.

title: Effective chemical potential and its phenomenological implications for the Hubble parameter
comment: 8 pages and 2 figures. Accepted for publication in Nuclear Physics B
summary: In cosmological models, the Hubble parameter is determined by the time evolution of the scale factor, and current observations reveal a persistent tension between its values inferred from different probes, such as Cepheid variable stars and the cosmic microwave background. Within Tsallis' statistical framework, we identify two distinct definitions of fugacity associated with relativistic and non-relativistic regimes. For the non-relativistic sector, we introduce an effective chemical potential and establish its connection with the Gibbs free energy. We then explore a phenomenological correspondence between this effective chemical potential and an Unruh-like temperature associated with accelerated trajectories in an expanding cosmological background. As an application, we derive an effective expression for the Hubble parameter that includes a statistics-dependent contribution arising from the non-relativistic matter sector. This contribution suggests that non-Gaussian statistical effects, when consistently incorporated in the non-relativistic matter sector, can enhance the sensitivity of the expansion rate to underlying thermostatistical assumptions, achieving a substantial increase in sensitivity by approximately ten orders of magnitude when compared with previous relativistic constructions that investigated, at a phenomenological level, the discrepancy observed in current determinations of the Hubble constant.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Tsallis-statistics-based framework linking non-relativistic effective chemical potential to an Unruh-like temperature in cosmology, yielding a modified Hubble parameter with statistics-dependent corrections that enhance sensitivity to thermostatistical assumptions by ~10 orders of magnitude—potentially addressing the Hubble tension.
AI.motivation: To address the persistent Hubble tension—discrepancy in H₀ measurements from local (e.g., Cepheids) vs. early-universe (e.g., CMB) probes—by exploring non-Gaussian statistical effects beyond standard Boltzmann–Gibbs statistics.
AI.method: Employs Tsallis' non-extensive statistical mechanics to define two fugacities (relativistic/non-relativistic); introduces an effective chemical potential for the non-relativistic sector linked to Gibbs free energy; establishes a phenomenological correspondence between this potential and an Unruh-like temperature arising from acceleration in expanding spacetime; derives a modified Hubble parameter incorporating a statistics-dependent correction from non-relativistic matter.
AI.result: Derives an effective Hubble parameter expression with a novel, non-Gaussian statistical contribution from non-relativistic matter; demonstrates that this contribution amplifies sensitivity to thermostatistical assumptions by ~10¹⁰ relative to prior relativistic Tsallis-based models.
AI.conclusion: Non-Gaussian statistical effects in the non-relativistic matter sector—via Tsallis statistics and Unruh-temperature correspondence—provide a theoretically grounded, highly sensitive mechanism to reconcile Hubble tension, surpassing sensitivity of earlier relativistic approaches.

title: Gravity Decoupling and Axionic Shift Symmetries
summary: We analyse the rôle of approximate axionic shift symmetries in gravity-decoupling limits arising in type II Calabi-Yau compactifications. Associated with each shift symmetry there is an axionic string whose tension constrains the gradient of the Kähler potential, as expected in regimes where gravity becomes weakly coupled. The gradients of these tensions define vector fields on moduli space, analogous to those associated with BPS particle masses. Together, they characterise the evolution of different effective field theory sectors along asymptotic limits, encoding both their coupling to gravity and their kinetic mixing. By deriving upper bounds on the inner products of these vector fields, we show that they split into mutually orthogonal subsets, one of which decouples from gravity. Finally, we relate the Laplacian of certain axionic string tensions to a divergent moduli space curvature.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how approximate axionic shift symmetries constrain effective field theories in type II Calabi-Yau compactifications when gravity decouples; it links axionic string tensions to Kähler potential gradients, identifies orthogonal vector fields on moduli space characterising gravity coupling and kinetic mixing, proves a subset decouples from gravity via inner-product bounds, and connects string tension Laplacians to divergent moduli space curvature.
AI.motivation: To understand how approximate axionic shift symmetries govern gravity-decoupling limits in string compactifications, particularly how they constrain low-energy effective field theories and their interplay with moduli space geometry and gravitational strength.
AI.method: Analytical study of type II Calabi-Yau compactifications using tools from supergravity, asymptotic Hodge theory, and moduli space geometry; derivation of constraints from axionic string tensions, computation of gradients and inner products of associated vector fields on moduli space, and analysis of the Laplacian of string tensions in relation to curvature.
AI.result: Axionic string tensions define moduli-space vector fields analogous to BPS mass vectors; inner-product bounds force their orthogonal decomposition, isolating a gravity-decoupled subset; the Laplacian of certain string tensions diverges precisely where moduli space curvature diverges.
AI.conclusion: Approximate axionic shift symmetries—via their associated strings—structurally organise asymptotic limits in Calabi-Yau compactifications: they encode both gravitational coupling and kinetic mixing, enforce orthogonality-based decoupling, and tie dynamical constraints directly to geometric singularities in moduli space.

title: Connection Factorization in Constrained Quantum Mechanics
summary: We investigate constrained quantum motion on curves and surfaces using connection factorization methods. We show that Laplace operators admit an exact half-connection factorization generated by connection one-forms. The first-order part of the Laplacian is identified with the Darboux rotational connection of the orthogonal frame. Elimination of this rotational connection naturally produces quadratic geometric invariants analogous to supersymmetric Riccati potentials. Using orthonormal moving frames, we derive effective geometric contributions for planar curves, spatial curves, and embedded surfaces. We further analyze Dirac reductions using structure equations and show that for Fermi-type reductions the scalar Jensen--Koppe--da Costa contribution is cancelled in the reduced Dirac sector, leaving a residual first-order spinorial derivative structure. The resulting framework suggests the existence of hidden nilpotent covariant differential complexes naturally generated by geometric connection structures.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a geometric framework for constrained quantum motion on curves and surfaces using connection factorization of Laplace operators, revealing supersymmetric-like Riccati-type geometric potentials and uncovering hidden nilpotent covariant differential complexes.
AI.motivation: To rigorously formulate quantum mechanics constrained to lower-dimensional manifolds (curves/surfaces) while preserving geometric covariance and uncovering underlying algebraic structures such as supersymmetry analogs and nilpotent complexes.
AI.method: Connection factorization of the Laplacian via orthonormal moving frames; identification of the first-order part with the Darboux rotational connection; derivation of effective geometric potentials using structure equations; Dirac reduction analysis with Fermi-type constraints.
AI.result: Exact half-connection factorization of the Laplacian; emergence of quadratic geometric invariants analogous to supersymmetric Riccati potentials; cancellation of the Jensen--Koppe--da Costa term in the Dirac sector under Fermi reduction; residual first-order spinorial derivative structure; indication of hidden nilpotent covariant differential complexes.
AI.conclusion: Geometric connection structures intrinsically encode both quantum confinement effects and algebraic supersymmetry-like features, suggesting a deeper covariant complex structure governing constrained quantum dynamics.
